ContinuousMap.norm_normalizeOfNoZero: Normalizing a bundled continuous map that is nonzero at every point produces a vector of norm one at every point. This uses a real normed vector space; no inner product, finite-dimensionality or nonempty-domain assumption is needed for this statement.
SphereTopology.eastVector_norm: The coordinate vector (1,0) has norm one in the Euclidean plane. This supplies the unit-circle membership proof for the east pole.
SphereTopology.eastPoint_first: The east pole has coordinate zero equal to one. The native display uses ofLp for Euclidean coordinate evaluation.
SphereTopology.eastPoint_second: The east pole has coordinate one equal to zero. Coordinates are indexed by Fin 2, starting at zero.
SphereTopology.eastPoint_ne_westPoint: The east and west poles of the literal real unit circle are distinct. This ensures their complements cover the circle.
SphereTopology.circlePunctured_join: The complement of the east pole and the complement of the west pole cover the entire circle, in that order. The opens lattice join is their union.
SphereTopology.circle_eq_east_or_west_of: A point of the literal unit circle whose second coordinate is zero is one of the east and west poles. The unit-norm hypothesis comes from the sphere subtype; the result is not a claim about arbitrary plane vectors.
SphereTopology.circlePunctureIntersectio: Removing both horizontal poles forces the second coordinate of every remaining circle point to be nonzero. This is the boundary fact used to split the intersection into its upper and lower components.
On the twice-punctured circle, component false means that the second coordinate is strictly positive: the upper component.
On the twice-punctured circle, component true means that the second coordinate is strictly negative: the lower component. The exclusion of both poles rules out the zero-coordinate boundary.
SphereTopology.continuous_circlePuncture: The upper/lower component selector is continuous to the discrete Boolean two-point space. Its two fibers are open in the twice-punctured circle; it is not asserted continuous on the whole circle.
SphereTopology.circlePunctureIntersectio: Selecting the component of the chosen north/south representative returns the original Boolean label. This is the exact right-inverse law of the component map.
The representative of the upper component false is the north pole and has second coordinate one.
The representative of the lower component true is the south pole and has second coordinate minus one.
For an upper-component point, the unnormalized segment from its north representative to the point has positive second coordinate at every time in the closed unit interval, including both endpoints.
For a lower-component point, the unnormalized segment from its south representative to the point has negative second coordinate at every time in the closed unit interval.
The interpolating vector never has zero second coordinate, since the segment stays in the selected upper or lower component. The time parameter is restricted to the unit interval.
The interpolating vector is nonzero at every allowed time. This justifies division by its norm in the radial homotopy.
The radial normalization of the nonzero interpolating vector has norm one, so it defines a point of the unit circle.
Radial normalization retains a nonzero second coordinate, so it does not hit either removed horizontal pole.
SphereTopology.continuous_circlePuncture: The unnormalized interpolation is jointly continuous in time and in the twice-punctured circle point. This is stronger than continuity for each fixed point separately.
The normalized interpolation is jointly continuous as a map into the twice-punctured circle. Nonvanishing of the interpolating vector makes the inverse norm continuous.
SphereTopology.circlePunctureIntersectio: At time zero the radial homotopy returns the selected north/south representative of the point's component, not the original point in general.
At time one the radial homotopy is the identity on the twice-punctured circle.
SphereTopology.circleEastPunctured_contr: The circle with its east pole removed is contractible, by its stereographic homeomorphism with the real line. This theorem supplies the class value rather than declaring a new global instance.
SphereTopology.circleWestPunctured_contr: The circle with its west pole removed is contractible, by its stereographic homeomorphism with the real line. This is a theorem-valued class witness, not a claim that the whole circle contracts.
SphereTopology.isZero_reducedSingularHom: Every nonnegative reduced integral singular homology object of the east-punctured circle is zero. The natural-number degree includes reduced degree zero; no degree minus one is represented.
Every nonnegative reduced integral singular homology object of the west-punctured circle is zero, using contractibility of that open.
SphereTopology.reducedSingularHomologyOn: The chosen H-tilde-one circle coordinate is the ordered east/west reduced connecting morphism followed by the upper/lower two-point homotopy equivalence and its fixed integer coordinate. The formula identifies the chosen map, not merely an unspecified isomorphism with the integers.
SphereTopology.circlePunctured_join_reve: The west/east ordering of the same two punctured opens also covers the circle. This changes the order of the Mayer--Vietoris input, not the underlying union.
SphereTopology.circlePunctureIntersectio: After the sign-free identification from the reversed meet ordering, label false still denotes a strictly positive second coordinate. Swapping cover order does not relabel the geometric upper component.
After the sign-free identification from the reversed meet ordering, label true still denotes a strictly negative second coordinate. The lower component keeps its Boolean label.
SphereTopology.reducedSingularHomologyOn: The reversed coordinate map uses the west/east connecting morphism, the same upper/lower component labels, and the fixed two-point integer coordinate. Its construction is displayed separately from the original ordered coordinate.
SphereTopology.circleReducedMayerVietori: Transporting the east/west reduced connecting morphism along the sign-free intersection swap gives the negative of the west/east connecting morphism. The minus sign belongs to ordered Mayer--Vietoris, not to a relabeling of upper and lower components.
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthVector_norm: The vector (0,0,1) has norm one in real Euclidean three-space. It therefore supplies the north pole of the literal unit two-sphere.
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthPoint_first: The north pole has coordinate zero equal to zero; the coordinate order is (x,y,z).
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthPoint_second: The north pole has coordinate one equal to zero.
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthPoint_third: The north pole has coordinate two equal to one. Fin 3 coordinates are numbered from zero.
SphereTopology.sphere2SouthPoint_first: The south pole has coordinate zero equal to zero, as the antipode of the north pole.
SphereTopology.sphere2SouthPoint_second: The south pole has coordinate one equal to zero.
SphereTopology.sphere2SouthPoint_third: The south pole has coordinate two equal to minus one.
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthPoint_ne_sout: The two poles are distinct, as witnessed by their third coordinates. Their complements consequently form an open cover.
SphereTopology.sphere2Punctured_join: The north-pole complement followed by the south-pole complement covers the literal two-sphere. This fixes the cover order used for the chosen homology coordinate.
SphereTopology.sphere2Punctured_join_rev: The south/north order of those same two punctured opens also covers the sphere. Ordered connecting-map formulas distinguish this order from north/south.
SphereTopology.sphere2_eq_north_or_south: A unit-sphere point with both first coordinates zero is a north or south pole. Its unit norm, encoded by the sphere subtype, forces the third coordinate to be plus or minus one.
SphereTopology.sphere2PunctureIntersecti: In the sphere with both poles removed, the first two coordinates cannot both vanish. This makes the projection toward the equator safe to normalize.
The unnormalized equatorial deformation keeps coordinate zero unchanged at every time.
The unnormalized equatorial deformation keeps coordinate one unchanged at every time.
Only coordinate two changes before normalization: it is multiplied by the unit-interval parameter t. Thus t=0 removes the vertical coordinate and t=1 restores it.
The vector (x,y,t*z) never vanishes on the twice-punctured sphere, because x and y are not both zero. This licenses radial normalization for every allowed t.
Normalizing the equatorial-deformation vector gives norm one, so it stays on the unit sphere.
Normalization does not make both first coordinates zero. The normalized homotopy therefore avoids both removed poles.
SphereTopology.continuous_sphere2Punctur: The map (t,p) to the unnormalized vector (x,y,t*z) is jointly continuous on the unit interval times the twice-punctured sphere.
The normalized deformation is jointly continuous into the twice-punctured sphere; the vector nonvanishing result supplies continuity of the inverse norm.
SphereTopology.sphere2PunctureIntersecti: At time zero the normalized vector has third coordinate zero. Its value lies on the literal equator.
SphereTopology.continuous_sphere2Punctur: The equatorial projection is continuous as a map into the equator subtype, not only after forgetting to ambient three-space.
SphereTopology.continuous_sphere2Equator: The literal equator includes continuously into the twice-punctured sphere; its zero third coordinate excludes both poles.
SphereTopology.sphere2PunctureIntersecti: At time zero the homotopy is equatorial projection followed by inclusion back into the puncture intersection.
At time one the normalized homotopy is the identity on the puncture intersection.
Projection after equator inclusion is exactly the identity on the equator. Along with the pointwise-fixed homotopy, this gives the stated equatorial homotopy equivalence.
SphereTopology.sphere2EquatorToCircleVec: The equator-to-circle coordinate map retains coordinate zero. It does not exchange the x and y axes.
The equator-to-circle coordinate map retains coordinate one, completing the prescribed (x,y) order.
SphereTopology.sphere1ToSphere2EquatorVe: The inverse coordinate construction inserts a circle point's coordinate zero as coordinate zero in three-space.
The inverse coordinate construction inserts a circle point's coordinate one as coordinate one in three-space.
The inverse coordinate construction inserts zero as coordinate two, placing its image on the equator.
SphereTopology.sphere2EquatorToCircleVec: Discarding the zero third coordinate of an equator point preserves unit norm. The two-coordinate vector is therefore a point of the standard circle.
SphereTopology.sphere1ToSphere2EquatorVe: Appending a zero third coordinate to a unit-circle point preserves norm one. This supplies the sphere membership proof for the inverse equator coordinate map.
SphereTopology.sphere2NorthPunctured_con: The sphere with its north pole removed is contractible through its stereographic homeomorphism with the Euclidean plane. This theorem returns the contractibility class witness.
SphereTopology.sphere2SouthPunctured_con: The sphere with its south pole removed is contractible through its stereographic homeomorphism with the Euclidean plane.
SphereTopology.isZero_reducedSingularHom: All nonnegative reduced integral homology objects of the north-punctured sphere are zero, using the contractibility witness.
All nonnegative reduced integral homology objects of the south-punctured sphere are zero. This is vanishing for the open, not for the full sphere.
SphereTopology.sphere2ReducedMayerVietor: The chosen reduced H2-to-H1 isomorphism is reduced-to-ordinary conversion, the north/south ordinary connecting morphism, the inverse intersection homology identification, and conversion back to reduced H1. Native _proof_1/_proof_2 tokens express the required positive-degree witnesses; they are not extra mathematical hypotheses.
SphereTopology.sphere2Antipodal_apply: The bundled antipodal self-map of the literal two-sphere evaluates by pointwise negation.
SphereTopology.sphere2Antipodal_north: The antipodal map sends the north pole to the south pole.
SphereTopology.sphere2Antipodal_south: The antipodal map sends the south pole back to the north pole. Thus it exchanges the ordered puncture cover.
SphereTopology.sphere2PunctureIntersecti: After forgetting the puncture and sphere subtype proofs, the antipodal map on the intersection is ordinary vector negation in E3.
SphereTopology.sphere2EquatorAntipodal_c: After forgetting the equator and sphere subtype proofs, equatorial antipodal negation is ordinary vector negation in E3.
SphereTopology.sphere2EquatorHalfTurnVec: The first coordinate of the equatorial half-turn is cos(pi*t)*x - sin(pi*t)*y. Together with the next coordinate law this specifies the rotation's orientation.
The second coordinate of the equatorial half-turn is sin(pi*t)*x + cos(pi*t)*y, with the same unit-interval time parameter.
The equatorial half-turn has third coordinate zero at every time, so it remains in the equatorial plane.
The half-turn preserves unit norm for an equator input. The trigonometric identity cos squared plus sin squared equals one supplies sphere membership.
SphereTopology.continuous_sphere2Equator: The equatorial half-turn is jointly continuous in its time parameter and equator point, as a map into the equator subtype.
SphereTopology.sphere2EquatorHalfTurnPoi: At time zero the equatorial rotation is the identity.
At time one the equatorial rotation reaches equatorial antipodal negation. This is a homotopy on the equator, not a homotopy from identity to antipodal on the full two-sphere.
SphereTopology.sphere2PunctureIntersecti: Applying antipodal negation after equatorial projection and re-inclusion agrees with projection, equatorial antipodal negation and re-inclusion. This identity is used to splice the equatorial half-turn with the radial deformation on the puncture intersection.
AlgebraicTopology.integralSingularHomolo: The map part of the degree-n integral singular homology functor is the homology map induced by the integer singular chain map. This identifies the functor presentation with the chain-complex presentation for any continuous map and any nonnegative degree.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_homology₀Iso: Under the coproduct description of zeroth simplicial homology, the class map of a zero-simplex is the coproduct inclusion of its connected component. The coefficient object is arbitrary in the category with coproducts, preadditive structure and homology appearing in the signature; this statement is not restricted to integer coefficients.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_homology₀Iso_asso: Generated by the reassoc attribute on homologyZeroPoint_homology₀Iso: the same component-inclusion formula after an arbitrary morphism from the component coproduct to Z. Both the arbitrary coefficient category and the added postcomposition are part of this statement.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_augmentation: The class map of a zero-simplex followed by the total augmentation is the identity of the coefficient object R. The supplied zero-simplex, rather than a global nonemptiness instance, supplies the point; the ambient category is as general as the displayed assumptions.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_augmentation_asso: Generated reassociated augmentation identity: composing the point class, augmentation and any morphism h from R to Z returns h. This is the postcomposition form of homologyZeroPoint_augmentation, with the same categorical hypotheses.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_naturality: A simplicial map sends the zeroth-homology class map of x to the class map of its image zero-simplex. This naturality statement uses the arbitrary coefficient object R and the displayed categorical homology assumptions.
SSet.homologyZeroPoint_naturality_assoc: Generated reassoc form of homologyZeroPoint_naturality: the point-class naturality square still agrees after any morphism from the target zeroth homology to Z. The extra codomain and postcomposition are explicit in the generated signature.
TopCat.singularHomologyZeroPoint_homolog: The integral H0 class map of a point becomes the inclusion of that point's path component in the coproduct description of singular H0. Coefficients are the universe-lifted integer module used by this file.

Generated reassociated point-component formula: after the H0 coproduct isomorphism and an arbitrary outgoing morphism, the point class equals the corresponding component inclusion followed by that morphism.
TopCat.singularHomologyZeroPoint_augment: A point class followed by the integral H0 augmentation is the identity on the lifted integer coefficient module. The theorem takes an actual point x and makes no separate path-connectedness assumption.
Generated reassoc form of the point-augmentation identity: following the point class and augmentation by any coefficient-module morphism h returns h.
TopCat.singularHomologyZeroPoint_natural: The ordinary integral H0 map of a continuous map sends the class map of x to the class map of f(x). No connectedness or nonemptiness beyond the supplied point is assumed.
Generated postcomposition form of singularHomologyZeroPoint_naturality, with an arbitrary morphism from the target space's ordinary integral H0 to Z.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_ι: The reduced H0 map, defined on the total-augmentation kernel, commutes with its kernel inclusion into ordinary integral H0. This holds for every continuous map, without a nonempty-space hypothesis.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_ι_: Generated reassoc form of the reduced-H0 kernel-inclusion naturality equation, after any morphism from the target's ordinary H0 to Z. This adds postcomposition rather than an extra topological assumption.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_id: The map induced on the augmentation kernel by the identity continuous map is the identity on reduced H0, for an arbitrary space.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_co: The reduced H0 map of a composite continuous map is the composite of the reduced H0 maps, in categorical composition order. No connectedness hypothesis is needed.
Generated reassociated composition law: the reduced H0 map of f followed by g, then any outgoing morphism h, equals the successive reduced maps followed by h.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroFuncto: Generated by the simps attribute on reducedSingularHomologyZeroFunctor. It identifies the functor's map on a continuous map with the explicitly constructed augmentation-kernel map reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap.
Generated by the simps attribute on reducedSingularHomologyZeroFunctor. Its object at X is precisely the total-augmentation kernel reducedSingularHomologyZero X, including for the empty space.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroInclus: The degree-zero inclusion from the file's reduced-homology convention to the ordinary integral H0 functor is a categorical monomorphism. This instance is inherited from the augmentation-kernel inclusion and needs no nonemptiness hypothesis.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyZeroToOrdi: The degree-zero reduced inclusion is a categorical monomorphism when its codomain is displayed using integralSingularHomology X 0. This is the same inclusion as reducedSingularHomologyZeroInclusion, with a definitionally equal presentation of ordinary homology.
TopCat.reducedSingularHomologyMap_isoOfN: In a specified nonzero natural-number degree, the reduced map agrees with the ordinary integral homology map under the canonical reduced-to-ordinary isomorphisms. The hypothesis n ≠ 0 is essential to this presentation.
Generated reassoc form of the nonzero-degree reduced-to-ordinary naturality equation. It retains n ≠ 0 and allows any subsequent morphism from the target's ordinary integral homology to Z.
TopCat.twoPointSwap_apply: The transposition of the canonical discrete two-point space Bool evaluates to Boolean negation. It swaps false and true in the fixed coordinate order.
TopCat.twoPointZerothHomotopyEquiv_mk: The component of b in the discrete Bool space is sent back to b by the chosen path-component equivalence. This fixes the labels used by the two-point H0 coordinates.
TopCat.singularHomologyZeroPoint_twoPoin: Under the ordered two-point ordinary H0 isomorphism, the class map of b becomes the coproduct inclusion indexed by b. The order is false, true; it is not chosen up to permutation.

TopCat.twoPoint_sigmaι_iso_inv: The inverse two-point H0 isomorphism sends the coproduct inclusion at b to the singular point-class map of b. This is the inverse-coordinate form of the fixed false/true presentation.
TopCat.twoPoint_sigmaι_iso_inv_assoc: Generated reassociated inverse-coordinate identity: the inclusion at b followed by the inverse H0 isomorphism and any outgoing morphism equals the class map of b followed by that morphism.
TopCat.twoPointSingularHomologyZeroIso_h: In the ordered two-point coproduct coordinates, summing the two coefficient components is exactly the ordinary H0 augmentation. Both coproduct summands are mapped by the identity coefficient morphism.

TopCat.twoPointReducedBasisClass_augment: The ordinary H0 class [false] − [true] has zero total augmentation. This is the kernel condition used to lift the chosen signed basis class to reduced H0.
Generated reassoc form of the signed basis class's zero-augmentation equation. The displayed right side is the zero morphism followed by the arbitrary outgoing morphism; no basis sign is changed.
TopCat.twoPointReducedBasis_ι: Including the chosen reduced basis into ordinary H0 gives the explicitly ordered difference [false] − [true]. This characterizes its lift through the augmentation kernel.
TopCat.twoPointReducedBasis_ι_assoc: Generated reassociated kernel-lift identity for the chosen two-point reduced basis, followed by any morphism from ordinary H0 to Z.
TopCat.twoPointReducedBasis_coordinate: Applying the false coordinate to the reduced basis [false] − [true] gives the identity coefficient morphism. This is one of the two inverse identities for the explicit reduced-H0 coordinate isomorphism.
TopCat.twoPointReducedBasis_coordinate_a: Generated reassoc form of the basis-then-coordinate identity: following these two maps by any coefficient-module morphism h returns h.
TopCat.twoPointReducedCoordinate_basis: Taking the false coordinate of a reduced H0 class and then multiplying the chosen basis [false] − [true] reconstructs that class. The augmentation-kernel condition supplies the relation between its two coordinates.
TopCat.mem_smallSingularSet_iff: A singular simplex belongs to the small singular subcomplex exactly when its continuous representative has range contained in one member of the family U. U may be any family of opens; this characterization does not require it to cover the space.
TopCat.smallSingularSetMap_comp_inclusio: The small-singular simplicial map induced by a continuous map respecting the two families of opens commutes with inclusion into all singular simplices. The hypothesis sends each source member into some target member; no covering hypothesis is used.

Generated reassoc form of small-singular simplicial-map compatibility with inclusion, followed by an arbitrary simplicial map from the target singular set. The family-respecting condition remains unchanged.
AlgebraicTopology.smallSingularChainMapO: A refinement from U to V induces a map of small integer chain complexes whose composite with the V-inclusion is the U-inclusion. Each U member need only lie in some V member; the families need not cover.

Generated reassoc form of refinement compatibility with inclusion, after any chain map from the full singular chain complex. The additional target complex and postcomposition are explicit in the signature.
AlgebraicTopology.smallSingularChainMap_: For a continuous map taking each U member into some V member, the induced map of small integer chains commutes with inclusion and the full singular chain map. Neither family is assumed to cover here.
Generated reassociated compatibility of the small-chain map with inclusion and the full singular chain map, followed by any chain map into Z. It retains the same family-respecting condition.
AlgebraicTopology.ι_chainGroupIsoFinsupp: The coefficient inclusion of a simplex followed by the chain-to-finsupp isomorphism is the linear singleton map at that simplex, composed with removal of the coefficient ULift. This is a morphism-level identity for any simplicial set and degree.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_h: Under the chain-to-finsupp isomorphism, the coefficient-one generator at a simplex is its finitely supported singleton with integer coefficient one. The lifted coefficient on the chain side is made explicit.
AlgebraicTopology.moduleCat_quasiIso_of_: A morphism of integer-module short complexes is a quasi-isomorphism if every target cycle is represented by an image cycle modulo a boundary and every source cycle whose image is a boundary is itself a boundary. The two displayed elementwise hypotheses are the surjectivity and injectivity criteria on homology; both complexes have the displayed homology instances.
AlgebraicTopology.sSetFinsuppBoundary_si: The boundary of a coefficient-one simplex is the sum of its faces, with integer sign (−1)^i on face i. The input degree is n+1, the output degree is n, and there are n+2 faces.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_s: Conjugating the simplicial integer-chain differential from degree n+1 to n by the two chain-to-finsupp isomorphisms yields the alternating-face linear boundary map. This is an equality of module morphisms for any simplicial set.
Elementwise form of chainGroupIsoFinsupp_sSet_d: transporting a finitely supported chain into the simplicial chain group, differentiating and transporting back is the alternating-face boundary.
AlgebraicTopology.mapDomain_smallFinsupp: Forgetting the smallness subtype commutes with the finitely supported alternating-face boundary. This holds for an arbitrary family U of opens, since the faces of a simplex small in U remain small in U.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_d: For a topological space's singular simplicial set, the transported integer-chain differential is singularFinsuppBoundary. This specializes the general simplicial chain-to-finsupp differential identity to singular chains.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_s: In finitely supported coordinates, inclusion of U-small singular chains is the integer-linear mapDomain along the small-simplex subtype inclusion. No open-cover hypothesis is needed for this morphism-level equality.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_d: Elementwise singular-chain specialization: transport a degree-(n+1) finitely supported chain to singular chains, take the differential and transport back to obtain its singularFinsuppBoundary.
AlgebraicTopology.chainGroupIsoFinsupp_s: Elementwise form of the small-chain inclusion coordinate identity: transport a finitely supported chain on small simplices into small chains and then all chains to obtain mapDomain along Subtype.val.
AlgebraicTopology.smallSingularChainIncl: In every nonnegative degree, the map including U-small integer singular chains into all singular chains is injective as a function. U may be any family of opens; surjectivity or an open-cover condition is not asserted.
AlgebraicTopology.mapDomain_smallChainOf: If every simplex in the support of c is small in U, then forgetting the subtype after restricting c with smallChainOfSupport recovers c. The support hypothesis is essential: without it the restriction discards non-small terms.
AlgebraicTopology.isCoverSmall_of_mem_ma: Every simplex in the support of a finitely supported chain obtained by forgetting the small-simplex subtype is small in U. This needs no assertion that U covers the entire space.
TopCat.openSingularSetMap_comp_inclusion: For a continuous map sending U into W, mapping the ambient open-singular subcomplex and then including it in the target singular set equals inclusion followed by the full singular-set map. This compatibility does not require a cover.

Generated reassoc form of openSingularSetMap_comp_inclusion: the same inclusion/naturality identity after an arbitrary simplicial map out of the target singular set. The MapsTo hypothesis is retained.
TopCat.openSingularSetInfMap_comp_left: The induced map between intersections of ambient open-singular subcomplexes commutes with projection to the first member. The underlying continuous map must send U into U' and V into V'; no cover hypothesis is used.
TopCat.openSingularSetInfMap_comp_left_a: Generated reassociated left-intersection compatibility, with arbitrary postcomposition from the target U' open-singular subcomplex to a simplicial set Z.
TopCat.openSingularSetInfMap_comp_right: The induced map between intersections of ambient open-singular subcomplexes commutes with projection to the second member V'. Both MapsTo hypotheses are explicit, without assuming the opens cover.
TopCat.openSingularSetInfMap_comp_right_: Generated reassoc form of the right-intersection compatibility, followed by any simplicial map from the target V' open-singular subcomplex to Z.
TopCat.openSingularSetMap_comp_supLeft: Mapping the first ambient open-singular subcomplex and then including it in the target union agrees with including in the source union and applying the induced union map. The ordered first member is U, and the pair need not cover.
TopCat.openSingularSetMap_comp_supLeft_a: Generated reassociated first-member/union naturality identity, after an arbitrary map from the target union of open-singular subcomplexes to Z.
TopCat.openSingularSetMap_comp_supRight: Mapping the second ambient open-singular subcomplex and then including it in the target union agrees with inclusion followed by the induced union map. The second member is V, with no cover assumption.
TopCat.openSingularSetMap_comp_supRight_: Generated reassoc form of the second-member/union naturality identity, retaining the ordered MapsTo hypotheses and allowing arbitrary postcomposition from the target union.
TopCat.openMap_comp_inclusion: Restricting a continuous map to U with values in W and then including W into Y is the original map after including U into X. The supplied MapsTo proof provides the restriction.
TopCat.openMap_comp_inclusion_assoc: Generated reassociated restriction/inclusion formula: the same equality remains true after any continuous map from Y to Z. No cover condition is added.

Generated reassoc form of the first intersection-inclusion identity, with an arbitrary continuous map from X to Z after the inclusion.

Generated reassociated difference-then-space zero identity, after any integer-module morphism from H_n(X;Z). The open-cover hypothesis and degree n are unchanged.
AlgebraicTopology.twoOpenMayerVietoris_t: For the open cover U union V = X, the map from the middle homology object in degree n+1 to ordinary H_(n+1)(X;Z), followed by the connecting morphism into intersection H_n, is zero. This records consecutive-map vanishing with the degree shift explicit.

Convexity.StdSimplex.affineChainIso_ι_as: Generated reassoc form of affineChainIso_ι: the coefficient inclusion and singleton map still agree after any integer-module morphism from the affine-chain coordinate module to Z.

Convexity.StdSimplex.affineBoundary_sing: The integer-linear affine boundary of a coefficient-one (n+1)-simplex is its explicitly signed alternating face chain affineBoundaryGenerator.
Convexity.StdSimplex.lsingle_comp_affine: Composing a simplex's integer-linear singleton inclusion with the explicit affine boundary gives the alternating sum of the singleton inclusions of its faces. The equality covers arbitrary input coefficients through linearity.

Convexity.StdSimplex.affineCone_single: The integer-linear cone operator sends a coefficient-one affine simplex to the coefficient-one simplex obtained by prepending the apex b. The degree increases by one.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineAugmentation_: The augmentation of a single affine zero-simplex with integer coefficient z is z. The vertex location does not affect augmentation.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.face_: Deleting vertex zero from the cone, whose apex is prepended, recovers the original ordered affine simplex. This fixes the positive first-face term in the cone boundary formula.
For a zero-simplex a, deleting vertex one from its cone to b leaves the zero-simplex at the apex b. This is the other endpoint in the degree-zero cone boundary formula.
Deleting vertex i+1 from the cone on a positive-dimensional affine simplex is the cone on the i-th face of the original simplex, with the same prepended apex.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.comp_: Affine composition commutes with taking a face in the parameter simplex: deleting a vertex before composition gives the same ordered simplex as deleting it afterward.
Pushing an affine cone through the affine map of a carries its apex x to affineMapMk a x and its base b to a.comp b. The apex remains the first vertex.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineBoundary_cone: For a coefficient-one affine simplex of positive degree, the boundary of its cone is the original chain minus the cone on its boundary. The degree-zero augmentation correction is handled by separate lemmas.
The boundary of the cone on a coefficient-one zero-simplex is that point chain minus the coefficient-one point chain at the apex. This records the endpoint sign explicitly.
For an arbitrary affine zero-chain c, the boundary of its cone equals c minus its total augmentation times the point chain at the apex. The augmentation term is essential in degree zero.
On affine chains of positive degree, the cone satisfies boundary(cone(c)) = c - cone(boundary(c)). The same fixed apex is used on both cone operators.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.comp_: The center of the affine composite a.comp b is the image under a's affine map of the center of b. Centers are equally weighted affine barycenters, so this is compatibility with affine composition.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mapAffineChain_sing: Pushforward of a coefficient-one affine simplex b along a is the coefficient-one simplex a.comp b. The linear pushforward may add coefficients for coincident images on general chains.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mapAffineChain_cone: Affine-chain pushforward commutes with coning when the apex is also mapped through the same affine map. The input chain can have arbitrary integer coefficients.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineSubdivision_s: The linear affine subdivision operator on a coefficient-one simplex agrees with the recursively defined signed subdivision subdivideSimplex of that simplex.
Convexity.StdSimplex.subdivideSimplex_ze: Signed barycentric subdivision leaves an affine zero-simplex unchanged as a coefficient-one chain. This is the base case of the recursive subdivision definition.
Convexity.StdSimplex.subdivideSimplex_su: Subdivision of a positive-dimensional affine simplex is the cone, with apex its center, on the linear subdivision of its oriented boundary. The integer alternating-face signs are retained.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mapAffineChain_subd: Signed subdivision of one affine simplex is natural under affine-chain pushforward: subdividing b and then mapping along a equals subdividing a.comp b.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineAugmentation_: The augmentation of the subdivision of an affine zero-simplex is one. This declaration retains its pre-simplification registration (simp↓), which is distinct from changing the mathematical statement or deleting the simp rule.
Linear affine subdivision preserves the total augmentation of every zero-chain. Coefficients may be arbitrary integers, not just one.
The signed boundary of an affine one-simplex has total augmentation zero: its two endpoint coefficients cancel.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineSubdivision_b: Affine subdivision commutes with the alternating-face boundary on every positive-degree affine integer chain. This is the chain-map identity, including the case of boundary into degree zero.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineHomotopy_sing: The integer-linear affine homotopy sends a coefficient-one simplex to its recursively constructed homotopySimplex chain in the next degree.
Convexity.StdSimplex.homotopySimplex_zer: The affine subdivision homotopy on a zero-simplex is the zero one-chain. Subdivision itself is already the identity in degree zero.
Convexity.StdSimplex.homotopySimplex_suc: In positive degree the affine homotopy is the cone to the simplex's center on the original simplex minus its subdivision minus the lower-degree homotopy of its boundary. This uses the id - Sd sign convention.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mapAffineChain_homo: The affine homotopy of a simplex commutes with affine-chain pushforward, in degree one higher than the input simplex. Its recursive centers and cones are mapped by the same affine map.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineHomotopy_degr: In degree zero, the boundary of the affine homotopy is c minus the subdivision of c. No negative-degree boundary/homotopy term is introduced.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineHomotopy_boun: For every positive-degree affine integer chain, boundary(H(c)) + H(boundary(c)) = c - Sd(c). This gives the homotopy between the identity and signed affine subdivision, in that order.
Convexity.StdSimplex.stdSimplex_dist_eq_: For the file's locally installed metric on the real standard simplex of a finite type, distance is exactly distance between the real weight functions. This fixes the metric used in all subsequent diameter estimates.
Convexity.StdSimplex.stdSimplexIsConvexD: The weight-induced metric on the real standard simplex of a finite type has convex distance. The source registers this named instance locally; the native theorem display does not mean the instance is globally registered for downstream typeclass search.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.verte: The diameter of the finite vertex set of any affine simplex is nonnegative, using the file's metric induced by real weight functions.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.dist_: The distance between any two specified vertices is at most the diameter of the simplex's finite vertex set. Repeated vertices and degenerate simplices are permitted.
For an affine n-simplex, the distance from its equally weighted center to any vertex is at most n/(n+1) times its vertex diameter. This also covers n = 0, where both sides vanish.
The center-to-point bound n/(n+1) times the vertex diameter holds for any affine combination of vertices chosen by v. The index map v need not be injective or preserve order.
Convexity.StdSimplex.exists_mem_support_: A nonzero coefficient in a finite sum of integer-valued finitely supported functions must occur in the support of at least one summand. The converse need not hold because coefficients can cancel.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineCone_eq_mapDo: Coning an affine chain is the finitely supported mapDomain along the function that prepends the fixed apex. This identifies the linear cone with coefficient-collecting pushforward.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mem_support_affineC: Every simplex with nonzero coefficient in a coned affine chain is the cone on some simplex in the original support, with the same apex. This is an existence implication, not an asserted equality of support sets.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.verti: Every vertex of an affine simplex lies in its own affine image, witnessed by the corresponding standard vertex. This uses the VerticesIn predicate's affine-image meaning.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.Verti: If all vertices of b lie in the affine image of a face of a, then they also lie in the affine image of a. The face inclusion supplies the domain reparametrization.
If b has all vertices in the affine image of a, coning b to the center of a preserves that property. The new apex is itself an affine combination of a's vertices.
Convexity.StdSimplex.subdivideSimplex_su: Every simplex in the support of the signed subdivision of a has all its vertices in the affine image of a. The vertices need not be original vertices of a.
Convexity.StdSimplex.homotopySimplex_sup: Every next-degree simplex in the support of the affine homotopy of a has all its vertices in the affine image of a. The statement is vacuous in degree zero, where the homotopy is zero.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.comp_: Under a.VerticesIn b, composing a with the classically chosen vertex-preimage simplex reconstructs b exactly. No uniqueness or injectivity of the chosen reparametrization is asserted.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.range: If every vertex of b lies in the affine image of a, the entire continuous affine image of b lies in that of a. The conclusion concerns all points, not only vertices.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.verte: Deleting a vertex cannot increase the vertex diameter of an affine simplex. This uses inclusion of the finite vertex sets and does not require a nondegenerate simplex.

Coning b to the center of an affine (n+1)-simplex a preserves the bound (n+1)/(n+2) times a's vertex diameter when b lies in the affine image of a specified face and already satisfies that bound. Both hypotheses are required.
Convexity.StdSimplex.subdivideSimplex_su: Each simplex surviving in the signed subdivision of an affine n-simplex has vertex diameter at most n/(n+1) times the original vertex diameter. The bound includes degenerate and zero-dimensional cases.
Convexity.StdSimplex.mem_support_affineS: A simplex in the support of the subdivision of a finite affine chain occurs in the subdivision support of some simplex in the original support. The result does not preclude cancellation between different input contributions.
Convexity.StdSimplex.affineSubdivision_i: If every simplex in the initial affine-chain support has vertex diameter at most D, each support simplex after N subdivisions has diameter at most (n/(n+1))^N times D. N may be zero; the hypothesis on the original support is explicit.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.dist_: The distance from the center of an affine n-simplex to any point of its affine image is at most n/(n+1) times the vertex diameter. This is the unreindexed version of the affine-combination estimate.
Convexity.StdSimplex.AffineSimplex.diam_: The metric diameter of the full affine image is at most twice the vertex diameter. This is the bound actually proved; it does not assert equality or the sharper vertex-diameter bound.
Convexity.StdSimplex.exists_affineSubdiv: For positive dimension n and epsilon > 0, some number N of subdivisions makes every support simplex of the standard coefficient-one n-simplex have affine-image diameter less than epsilon. The theorem is existential, not a chosen numerical algorithm for N.

Given an open cover of any topological space and one continuous singular simplex, some subdivision of its standard domain has every surviving affine piece mapped into a cover member. The member may depend on the piece; no metric on the target space is assumed.
AlgebraicTopology.singularFinsuppMap_sin: Postcomposition of a coefficient-one singular simplex by a continuous map is the coefficient-one image simplex in the target singular set. This is the generator formula for integer-linear singular-chain pushforward.
AlgebraicTopology.mem_support_realizeAff: Every singular simplex with nonzero coefficient after realizing an affine chain through x comes from some affine simplex in the original support. Distinct affine pieces may realize to the same singular simplex, so this is only the stated support implication.
AlgebraicTopology.affinePostcompose_rang: Precomposing a singular simplex x with an affine parameter map produces a singular simplex whose range is contained in the range of x. Despite its name, affinePostcompose performs this domain precomposition.
AlgebraicTopology.realizeAffineChain_sin: Realizing the coefficient-one affine simplex a through a singular simplex x gives the coefficient-one singular simplex affinePostcompose x a. The resulting degree is the dimension of a.
AlgebraicTopology.affinePostcompose_natu: Continuous postcomposition on the target space commutes with the affine domain precomposition used to form affinePostcompose. Both operations give the same resulting singular simplex.
AlgebraicTopology.singularFinsuppMap_rea: Realization of an affine chain is natural under continuous maps of target spaces: postcompose the realized chain, or postcompose the outer singular simplex before realization. The equality holds for arbitrary integer coefficients.
AlgebraicTopology.affinePostcompose_stan: Precomposing a singular simplex with the standard affine simplex leaves it unchanged. The standard affine map is the identity on the domain simplex.
AlgebraicTopology.affinePostcompose_face: Realizing a face of the affine parameter simplex gives the corresponding singular face of the realized simplex. The same deleted-vertex index is used on both sides.
AlgebraicTopology.affinePostcompose_comp: Realization of an affine composite agrees with successive affine precompositions of the singular simplex. The dimension indices record the two domain changes.
AlgebraicTopology.realizeAffineChain_map: Realizing a chain after affine-chain pushforward along a equals realizing it directly through the singular simplex affinePostcompose x a. This is the linear-chain form of compatibility with affine composition.
AlgebraicTopology.singularFinsuppBoundar: The boundary of a coefficient-one singular (n+1)-simplex is the sum of its n-faces with integer coefficient (-1)^i at face i. This fixes the orientation convention for the finitely supported singular chains.
Realization commutes with boundary: the singular boundary of a realized affine chain is the realization of its affine boundary. Both differentials lower degree by one with the same alternating signs.
AlgebraicTopology.AffineSimplex.comp_sta: Composing an affine simplex with the standard affine simplex of its domain gives the original affine simplex. The actual declaration is in AlgebraicTopology.AffineSimplex; this note does not rename it into Convexity.StdSimplex.
AlgebraicTopology.realize_subdivide_face: Subdividing a face of the standard domain simplex and realizing through x agrees with realizing the subdivision of the lower-dimensional standard simplex through the corresponding singular face of x. The result has degree n.
AlgebraicTopology.realize_homotopy_face_: Applying the affine homotopy to a standard face and realizing through x agrees with realization through the corresponding singular face of the standard lower-dimensional homotopy. The degree-raising homotopy produces chains of degree n+1.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivisionIte: Zero iterations of singular subdivision give the identity integer-linear map on chains of the chosen degree. This is distinct from the zero initial value of the iterated homotopy.
The (N+1)-fold subdivision map first performs one subdivision and then the N-fold iterate, as expressed by linear-map composition. The chain degree stays fixed.

Applying the recursively defined linear singularSubdivisionIterate equals N-fold function iteration of singularSubdivision on the input chain. This relates the linear-map and function-iterate presentations.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivision_si: Subdivision of a coefficient-one singular simplex is obtained by realizing the signed subdivision of its standard affine domain through that simplex. General chains are treated by integer linearity.
AlgebraicTopology.mem_support_singularSu: Every simplex in a subdivided chain's support has range contained in the range of some simplex in the original support. This is a local range-control statement and assumes no open cover.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivision_re: Singular subdivision of a realized affine chain equals realization of the affine subdivision of that chain. The outer singular simplex is unchanged.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivision_it: N-fold singular subdivision of a coefficient-one singular simplex is realization of N-fold affine subdivision of the coefficient-one standard domain simplex. The equality includes N = 0.
AlgebraicTopology.exists_singularSubdivi: For a given singular simplex and an open cover, some subdivision iterate has every support simplex contained in a cover member. The exponent is allowed to depend on the original simplex and the cover.
AlgebraicTopology.isCoverSmall_of_mem_si: If every simplex in a chain's support is small in the family U, then every simplex after one subdivision is also small in U. The family need not cover the whole space; range containment suffices.
Smallness of a finite chain in an arbitrary family of opens is preserved by every subdivision iterate. No open-cover hypothesis is required for this preservation result.

If all support simplices are small after N subdivisions, they remain small after any M subdivisions with N <= M. U may be any family of opens; this is persistence of an already established smallness condition.
AlgebraicTopology.exists_singularSubdivi: For any finitely supported singular integer chain and an actual open cover, there is one exponent N making every simplex in the subdivided chain's support small. N depends on that finite chain and cover, not uniformly on all chains.
AlgebraicTopology.singularHomotopy_singl: The singular subdivision homotopy on a coefficient-one simplex is realization of the affine homotopy of its standard domain. It raises degree by one.
AlgebraicTopology.mem_support_singularHo: Every next-degree simplex in a singular homotopy chain has range contained in that of some input support simplex. This support control is independent of a cover hypothesis.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivision_bo: Singular subdivision commutes with the finitely supported singular boundary on all positive-degree chains. The subdivisions on the two sides operate in consecutive degrees.
AlgebraicTopology.singularSubdivisionIte: Every N-fold singular subdivision commutes with boundary. The same number N of subdivisions is used before and after lowering the degree.
AlgebraicTopology.singularHomotopy_degre: For a singular zero-chain, the boundary of its subdivision homotopy is c minus Sd(c). There is no additional negative-degree term; subdivision is the identity in this degree.
AlgebraicTopology.singularHomotopy_bound: For a positive-degree singular chain, boundary(H(c)) + H(boundary(c)) = c - Sd(c). This realizes the affine homotopy identity with the identity-minus-subdivision sign.
AlgebraicTopology.singularHomotopyIterat: The telescoping homotopy associated to zero subdivisions is the zero degree-raising linear map. It is not the identity map or a zero-fold function iterate of singularHomotopy.
The homotopy for N+1 subdivisions is H plus the homotopy for N subdivisions applied after one subdivision. This is a sum of degree-raising linear maps, not self-composition of H.
In degree zero, the boundary of the telescoping homotopy for N subdivisions equals c minus Sd^N(c). The equality includes N = 0.

The telescoping singular homotopy satisfies boundary(H_N(c)) + H_N(boundary(c)) = c - Sd^N(c) on every positive-degree chain. This supplies the homotopy identity for the subdivision iterate, with the same N in both degrees.
AlgebraicTopology.mem_support_singularHo: Every simplex surviving in the telescoping homotopy for N subdivisions has range contained in an original input support simplex's range. The statement covers every N and does not require an open cover.
AlgebraicTopology.isCoverSmall_of_mem_si: If an input chain is small in a family U, every simplex in the iterated homotopy chain remains small in U. This is a preservation statement for arbitrary families, not the separate existence theorem requiring an open cover.
